statement: Each 64-bit counter increments by the step value whenever the prescaler times out.
Each timer generates an interrupt if its counter reaches or exceeds the programmed value.
The tick generator creates a tick every time its internal counter hits the CFG0.prescaler value.
Each tick increments mtime by the CFG0.step value.
The timer compares 64-bit mtime with 64-bit mtimecmp and raises an interrupt when mtime is greater than or equal to mtimecmp.
Each hart has its own tick generator and counter, so the number of prescaler, step, and mtime registers equals the number of harts.
The IP is fixed to one hart and one timer per hart.
There are separate interrupts per timer and a set of interrupt enable and state registers per hart.
The prescaler and step fields must be stable for the timer value to increment correctly.
Software should de-activate the timer before changing the prescaler or step fields, then proceed with the change.
mtimecmp shall be written after mtime in order to clear any pending interrupt condition.
Software may set mtimecmp to 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF to get an intermediate interrupt.
Setting mtimecmp to 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF - step + 1 works for the intermediate interrupt, since the last mtime before wrap is at least that large.
The RV_TIMER module generates the interrupt when mtime is greater than or equal to mtimecmp.
The interrupt can be cleared by writing 1 to the Interrupt Status register INTR_STATE0.
The interrupt can be cleared by updating mtimecmp; a write to either COMPARE_LOWER0_0 or COMPARE_UPPER0_0 clears the interrupt source.
ALERT_TEST register must be located at offset 0x0 with length 4 bytes.
CTRL must be at offset 0x4, length 4, reset to 0x0 with reset mask 0x1.
INTR_ENABLE0 must be at offset 0x100, length 4, reset to 0x0 with reset mask 0x1.
INTR_STATE0 must be at offset 0x104, length 4, reset to 0x0 with reset mask 0x1.
INTR_TEST0 must be at offset 0x108, length 4, reset value 0x0 with reset mask 0x1.
CFG0 must be at offset 0x10c, length 4, reset to 0x10000 with reset mask 0xff0fff.
TIMER_V_LOWER0 at offset 0x110 holds timer value [31:0] as rw field v, reset 0x0, mask 0xffffffff.
TIMER_V_UPPER0 at offset 0x114 holds timer value [63:32] as rw field v, reset 0x0, mask 0xffffffff.
COMPARE_LOWER0_0 at offset 0x118 holds compare value [31:0] as rw field v, reset 0xffffffff, mask 0xffffffff.
COMPARE_UPPER0_0 at offset 0x11c holds compare value [63:32] as rw field v, reset 0xffffffff, mask 0xffffffff.
ALERT_TEST must reset to 0x80000000 with reset mask 0x80000001.
Writing 0 to regwen disables alert testing until the next reset; regwen can only be cleared, not set, by writes.
Writing 1 to fatal_fault triggers one alert event of the fatal kind.
When active_0 is 1 the timer operates; bits 31:1 of CTRL are reserved.
IE_0 (bit 0, rw, reset 0x0) is the interrupt enable for the timer; bits 31:1 are reserved.
IS_0 (bit 0, rw1c, reset 0x0) holds the timer interrupt status and is cleared by writing 1; bits 31:1 are reserved.
T_0 (bit 0, wo, reset x) is the interrupt test for timer; bits 31:1 are reserved.
CFG0 step (bits 23:16, rw, reset 0x1) is the increment per tick; prescale (bits 11:0, rw, reset 0x0) generates the tick; other bits reserved.
The racl_policies input must carry the incoming RACL policy vector from a racl_ctrl instance, with the policy selection vector parameter selecting the policy for each register.

not_verified.note: The DUT interface has no racl_policies port, and RACL is disabled (RT-1-02).

statement: The module must raise interrupt timer_expired_hart0_timer0 when hart0's timer0 has expired (mtime >= mtimecmp).
The fatal_fault alert must be triggered when a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault is detected inside RV_TIMER.
The design under verification has exactly one hart and one timer (N_HARTS = 1, N_TIMERS = 1).
Every register access is permitted when RACL is disabled.
The alert sender of rv_timer and the alert receiver of the wrapper both use the synchronous clocking scheme, with no synchronizer flops on the differential pairs.

not_verified.note: The alert sender/receiver clocking scheme is a structural choice inside the wrapper.

statement: Every run uses the single fixed configuration; there is no design parameter to vary.

not_verified.note: There is a single fixed configuration and no parameter to sweep.

statement: All inputs are sampled and all outputs change at the rising edge of clk_i, except for the effect of rst_ni.
rst_ni is active-low and may be asserted asynchronously, but its release must be synchronous to clk_i.
Every register holds its reset value as given in the rv_timer specification register tables.
i_a_opcode must encode TL-UL request types as Get = 4, PutFullData = 0 and PutPartialData = 1.
i_a_instr = 1 marks the request as an instruction fetch (a_user.instr_type = MuBi4True); i_a_instr = 0 marks a data access (MuBi4False).
When i_a_intg_flip is 1, the A-channel integrity sent with the request is corrupted.
o_d_opcode must encode TL-UL response types as AccessAck = 0 and AccessAckData = 1.
o_d_intg_err indicates that the response integrity of the D-channel beat is wrong.
o_alert indicates that the alert fatal_fault was received.
o_alert_integ_fail indicates a signal integrity failure on the alert differential pairs.
The i_a_*, o_a_ready, o_d_* (except o_d_intg_err) and i_d_ready ports must be the same-named fields of the rv_timer TL-UL device interface tl, with TL-UL meaning.
a_user.instr_type is MuBi4True when i_a_instr is 1 and MuBi4False when i_a_instr is 0.

not_verified.note: a_user.instr_type is generated inside the wrapper. Its effect is exercised by CHK-021.

statement: The test bench must follow the TL-UL host rules, including keeping A-channel signals stable while a_valid is 1 and a_ready is 0.
The test bench may send requests listed as TL-UL error cases (unsupported opcode, bad size or mask, misaligned address) as legal stimulus.
The device must answer such error-case requests with d_error = 1.
The wrapper must compute a_user.cmd_intg and a_user.data_intg with the OpenTitan TL-UL host integrity generator, so the request carries correct integrity.
Bit 0 of a_user.cmd_intg must be inverted.

not_verified.note: The inverted cmd_intg bit is internal. Its consequence (the fatal alert) is checked by CHK-016.

statement: Such a request is a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault that triggers the fatal_fault alert.
o_d_intg_err must be 1 in a cycle where o_d_valid is 1 and the d_user.rsp_intg check fails, and 0 otherwise.
A correct device must never make o_d_intg_err 1.
rv_timer has one alert, fatal_fault, sent through an alert sender.

not_verified.note: The single alert and its sender are structural. Alert behaviour is checked by CHK-014 and CHK-016.

statement: o_alert is the receiver's alert_o output and is 1 for one clock cycle for each alert handshake the receiver detects.
A correct sender never makes o_alert_integ_fail 1.
o_alert pulses repeatedly after a bus integrity fault until rst_ni is asserted, as a fatal alert is repeated until reset.
A write of 1 to ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault triggers exactly one alert event.
o_intr_timer_expired must behave as an event-type interrupt per the comportability specification, with registers INTR_ENABLE0, INTR_STATE0 and INTR_TEST0.
Verification shall cover reset values of every register through the ports.
Verification shall cover the access type of every register field as given in the register tables (rw, rw1c, wo, rw0c).
Verification shall cover the tick generator (prescaler) and the step.
Verification shall cover counting of the 64-bit timer value, including writes to it and the carry from the lower to the upper half.
Verification shall cover the compare and the interrupt: state, enable, test, and clearing by writing the compare registers.
Verification shall cover ALERT_TEST with its regwen field.
Verification shall cover bus error responses (unmapped addresses, sub-word writes, instruction fetches, integrity errors) and the fatal_fault alert.
Behaviour close to 2^64 shall be reached by writing the timer value registers.
Timer value increases by CFG0.step (modulo 2^64) once every CFG0.prescale + 1 cycles; prescale 0 gives a tick every cycle.
The first tick shall come no later than CFG0.prescale + 1 + 4 cycles after the write response.
Tests write CFG0 and TIMER_V_* only while CTRL.active_0 = 0; behaviour after such a write while active is not checked.
INTR_STATE0.IS_0 shall read 1 within 4 cycles after a write of 1 to it.
IS_0 shall be 1 no later than 4 cycles after that tick.
IS_0 shall be 1 no later than CFG0.prescale + 1 + 4 cycles after the write response.
o_intr_timer_expired shall equal IS_0 AND IE_0.
IS_0 shall be 0 and the interrupt deasserted within 4 cycles.
IS_0 shall be 1 again within 4 cycles; an intermediate dip is not checked.
Write-only fields read 0, reserved bits read 0 and writes to them have no effect.
INTR_TEST0 reads 0x0 and ALERT_TEST reads 0x8000_0000.
Regwen reads 0 until reset; a later write of 0x8000_0001 completes with d_error = 0, triggers no alert.
Exactly one o_alert pulse shall occur, no later than 16 cycles after the write response.
At least one o_alert pulse and no more pulses than writes shall occur.
Tests do not use the combined write 0x0000_0001; they write 0x8000_0001.
o_alert shall pulse no later than 16 cycles after acceptance, then at least once every 32 cycles until rst_ni is asserted.
The test resets the design.
A write with i_a_instr = 1 is not used.
The slave returns d_error = 1 and changes no register.
Requests at offset 0x200 and above are not used.
Returns d_error = 1 and changes nothing.
Completes with d_error = 0 and has the effect of the write.
The write succeeds with d_error = 0.
Match responses by d_source, use distinct a_source per outstanding request, and do not assume o_a_ready = 1.
Returned value lies between values before the request and after the response.
d_error is correct, d_source echoes a_source, d_size echoes a_size, d_opcode is AccessAckData for Get and AccessAck for PutFullData and PutPartialData.
d_error = 1 is returned.
The test bench keeps i_a_valid = 0.
o_d_valid, o_alert, o_alert_integ_fail and o_intr_timer_expired shall be 0.
The pending response is discarded.
o_d_intg_err and o_alert_integ_fail shall be 0 in every cycle.
Reached only by writing the timer value registers while inactive to values near the carry, then counting.
Tests drive i_a_param = 0.
Existing TL-UL IP blocks may be used directly in devices that do not need the additional sideband signals.

not_verified.note: This is about reusing base TL-UL IP. The wrapper produces the sideband (user) signals.

statement: The bus carries only one request and one response per cycle, and no burst transactions.
Bus primitives, hosts and peripherals developed with the extended specification can be used with blocks using the base specification.

not_verified.note: This is about compatibility between base and extended blocks. User bits are out of scope (D-019).

statement: As a receiver, a baseline block ignores the user signals.

not_verified.note: This binds the interconnect's request steering. There is no fabric between the test bench and the DUT.

not_verified.note: This is general advice on user-bit usage. User-bit layout is out of scope (D-019).

not_verified.note: This binds the bus fabric.

statement: a_opcode may designate a write (Put) or read (Get); writes may be full (PutFullData) or partial (PutPartialData).

For PutFullData, a_size should be 'h2 for a 32b write ('h3 for 64b bus).
For PutPartialData, a_size should encode 2^a_size bytes and the a_mask bits should indicate the valid byte lanes.
Devices should return an error for undefined request opcodes.
Undefined response opcodes d_opcode 3'b01x and 3'b1xx should return an error.
TL-UL devices must raise a runtime error via d_error when a request carries a wrong opcode.
a_size must not be greater than 2; a request violating this is flagged by the device with d_error.
Inactive lanes must be marked with 'b0 in a_mask; violation is flagged by the device with d_error.
PutFullData must mark all active lanes with a 'b1 in a_mask; violation is flagged by the device with d_error.
TL-UL devices must raise a runtime error via d_error for accesses to non-existent addresses.
Register files always assume aligned 32-bit accesses, so accesses to them must be aligned 32-bit.
A host must discard orphaned responses (no valid request counterpart) and responses with the wrong opcode.
Devices and hosts may implement additional, more restrictive checks if needed.

not_verified.note: This concerns port naming.

not_verified.note: This concerns port naming.

not_verified.note: This is an hjson limit.

statement: INTR_STATE at offset 0x0 holds interrupt state, INTR_ENABLE at 0x4 masks it to intr_o, INTR_TEST at 0x8 is write-only and asserts the interrupt.
INTR_STATE shows raw latched interrupt events and is not qualified by INTR_ENABLE.
The interrupt is cleared only by a software W1C write of the INTR_STATE bitfield.
Interrupt requests are triggered while input is true, including immediately after the previous request is acknowledged.

not_verified.note: This is Status-type behaviour. rv_timer has only an Event-type interrupt (designer decision, D-019).

statement: When the event occurs it is latched into the INTR_STATE bitfield and intr_o is latched high until acknowledged, then low.
A status type interrupt must drive a wired level-triggered interrupt directly from the hardware input signal, qualified only by INTR_ENABLE, staying asserted while the input is asserted.

not_verified.note: This is a Status-type interrupt rule, out of scope by designer decision.

statement: The wired status interrupt must not deassert until the root cause of the hardware input signal is addressed by software intervention.

not_verified.note: This is a Status-type interrupt rule, out of scope by designer decision.

statement: Software cannot acknowledge a status type interrupt through INTR_STATE, which is read-only (ro) in this context.

not_verified.note: This is a Status-type interrupt rule, out of scope by designer decision.

statement: Software should mask the interrupt, at the peripheral or further up the tree such as the PLIC.

not_verified.note: This is software advice for Status-type interrupts.

statement: Masking at the peripheral can be achieved by clearing the corresponding bit in INTR_ENABLE.
The event must set the associated bit in INTR_STATE to 1.
A write of 1 to the associated foo bit of INTR_TEST can set the corresponding INTR_STATE bit.
The outgoing interrupt intr_foo_o must be the INTR_STATE output ANDed with INTR_ENABLE.
A write of 1 to an INTR_STATE bit clears the latched value, but INTR_STATE returns to true if the event is still active.
Hardware must not clear the latched interrupt state; only software can clear it.
A recoverable alert must be one-time triggered: the alert sender transmits a single alert event when the error condition is asserted.

not_verified.note: rv_timer has no recoverable alert.

not_verified.note: This is a recommendation about local countermeasures. None are specified for rv_timer.

not_verified.note: This concerns alert naming.

not_verified.note: This concerns internal reg2hw struct contents.
